project.title: Native purpose-bound email token prerequisite
project.goal: Provide bounded source-readable HS256 metadata for future one-time native email verification
project.scope: Crypto only, no user/issuance database mutation, HTTP/mail or email-verification authority

boundary.responsibility: Sign and verify purpose/workspace/key/time-bound email-token metadata
boundary.rationale: Future admitted one-time verification needs explicit native context claims instead of stateless source authority
excludes: Database issuance/consumption, current-user mutation, HTTP/mail, legacy coexistence and deployment

scenario.normal.description: Native tokens are accepted by installed jose/source reader, and actual source signer emits a native-compatible bound envelope

scenario.given: Native crypto and installed source/JWT oracle on synthetic metadata
scenario.when: Issue or verify an email token
scenario.then: Native tokens are accepted by installed jose/source reader, and actual source signer emits a native-compatible bound envelope

scenario.refusal.description: Strict canonical compact encoding, signed duplicate/unknown fields, wrong key/workspace/purpose/nonce and change-email envelopes refuse

errors.refused: Fixed AuthError, no raw bearer/claim/parser text

preconditions: Trusted active key/workspace and Clock, not request-supplied time/configuration
Future consumer must bind native issuance/current user and recheck time under admitted writer; legacy endpoint cannot bypass context
postconditions: Metadata only, never an authenticated principal or verified user
Source-readable HS256 envelope with mandatory native purpose/workspace/random nonce and exact hour
external_effects: OS entropy and trusted Clock sampling only; no database/filesystem/network/user mutation

authorization.rationale: Do not confuse a valid signature or key/workspace proof binding with current user authority, freshness at later consumption, replay prevention or safe legacy coexistence.
